artworks.title: Heracles Kills Periclymenus in the Form of an Eagle
artworks.description: Isaac Briot's engraving for an Ovidian Metamorphoses cycle shows Heracles striking down Periclymenus as the Neleid shape-shifter takes eagle form at the sack of Pylos. Poseidon's gift of metamorphosis cannot save Neleus' son when Heracles hunts the Pylian house.

artworks.title: Ship of Periclymenus
artworks.description: A Cooper Hewitt print from the 1608 Medici wedding naval pageant: the allegorical Ship of Periclymenus sails among mythic vessels staged for Cosimo II. Florentine festival culture gives the shape-shifting Argonaut a floating emblem beside the Argo's other names.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Apollonius names Periclymenus son of Neleus among the Argonauts — Poseidon granted him every shape, a gift that later fails against Heracles at Pylos.

popCulture.title: Periclymenus
popCulture.description: Shape-shifting son of Neleus — Argonaut and victim of Heracles' sack of Pylos, not the Theban namesake.

popCulture.title: Neleus
popCulture.description: Periclymenus' father — king of Pylos whose house Heracles destroys, leaving Nestor as the surviving Neleid.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus records Poseidon's gift of metamorphosis and Heracles' killing of Periclymenus among Neleus' sons at Pylos.
